alternatives.reason: Higher security class (pqc vs hybrid-pqc) but only 3 ready endpoints (peer-01, peer-02, peer-06) since peer-04 and peer-05 lack kem:mlkem768; objective prioritizes maximum endpoint count first, so this profile yields fewer migrated endpoints and is not selected.
This is the asset's current profile (classical security class, below the hybrid-pqc security floor); excluded per task instructions not to propose the existing profile and per policy security floor.

proposal.rationale: Comparing allowlisted PQC-capable profiles against peer capabilities (excluding peer-03 per engineering note on decommissioning): tls13-hybrid-x25519-mlkem768 (requires kem:x25519mlkem768) has 4 ready endpoints with confirmed readiness (peer-01, peer-02, peer-04, peer-06), while tls13-mlkem768 (requires kem:mlkem768) has only 3 (peer-01, peer-02, peer-06). Since the task's primary objective is to maximize the number of ready endpoints migrated, the hybrid profile is selected despite tls13-mlkem768 having a higher security class (pqc vs hybrid-pqc); the tie-breaker on security class only applies among profiles achieving the same maximum endpoint count, which is not the case here. Both candidate profiles use liboqs-0.16.0, which is present on the asset, satisfying the implementation requirement. peer-05 (only classical x25519 capability) is not included as it does not advertise the required capability for either PQC profile; peer-03 is intentionally excluded per the engineering note despite having compatible capabilities. All included/excluded peers have confirmed ('known') readiness, so there are no unresolved dependencies. This migration should be executed within the Tuesday 02:00-04:00 UTC change window with handshake error-rate monitoring for 30 minutes post-change per the rollback procedure, and the on-call network team should be the rollback owner of record in the ticket.
